Mali.title: Mali: the army announces that it hit two bases on the same day, localized war material
Mali.summary: Two strikes in a single day, on two remote areas: the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) claim to have targeted two bases of armed groups in Mali on Saturday, October 17, 2026. The General Staff of the Armed Forces has announced this since Bamako, specifying that these actions are part of Operation Dougoukoloko. One of the targets is 100 km northwest of Menaka, the capital of an eastern region of the country .

Mali.title: Operation Dougoukoloko: two terrorist bases targeted near Diafarabé and Menaka
Mali.summary: Operation Dougoukoloko: two targeted terrorist bases near Diafarabé and Menaka The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by their partners, targeted two bases presented as terrorist in the Diafarabé and Menaka sectors on Saturday, October 17, 2026, as part of Operation Dougoukoloko, according to the General Staff of the Armed Forces According to the press release, the first position was located 40 km northeast of Diafarabé thanks to precise information.

Mali.title: Kayes: four suspects arrested for theft from gold mining sites
Mali.summary: Kayes: four suspects arrested for robberies at gold mining sites The National Police arrested four people as part of the "Kokadjè" operation in Sadiola, in the Kayes region. They are suspected of being involved in several robberies targeting gold miners and local residents . The operation, carried out on the night of 6 to 7 October 2026 by the Sadiola police station, identified a 28-year-old suspect, presented as the alleged leader of the group.

Mali.title: Hydrocarbon refuelling: A third convoy of 734 tankers arrives in Bamako
Mali.summary: Hydrocarbon refueling: A third convoy of 734 tanker trucks arrives in Bamako This Saturday, October 17, at around 6 a.m., a new convoy of 734 tanker trucks reached Bamako, escorted by the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa). This is the third major procurement of the month, following those of October 3 and 10. At the same time, the regions continue to be supplied .

Mali.title: Sadiola: Four suspects arrested by the police during Operation "Kokadjè"
Mali.summary: The fight against crime and delinquency continues in the Kayes region. As part of the "Kokadjè" operation, the Sadiola Police Station, headed by Chief Police Commissioner Ibrahima Abdina GUINDO, arrested four (04) individuals suspected of being involved in several alleged acts of theft to the detriment of gold miners and local populations . This operation, carried out on the night of 6 to 7 October 2026, is part of the dynamic driven by the Regional Director of the National Police of Kayes, the Chief Police Controller Tapa Oury DIOLLO.

Mali.title: Refuelling: Bamako welcomes a new record 734 tanker convoy
Mali.summary: Fuel supply: the pace does not slow down! This Saturday, October 17, 2026, at around 6 a.m., a new convoy of 734 tanker trucks arrived in Bamako, escorted by our valiant Malian Armed Forces (FAMa). This is the third convoy to reach the capital since the beginning of October, after those of October 3 and 10.

Mali.title: West Africa: Faced with terrorism, Bamako and Abidjan share a common struggle
Mali.summary: After Abidjan's outstretched hand to the ESA countries, the Ivorian intelligence chief is staying in Bamako to relaunch security cooperation. The Ivorian National Intelligence Coordinator, Vassiriki Traoré, is currently in Bamako at the invitation of his Malian counterpart, General Modibo Koné, Director of the National Agency for State Security (ANSE) . On the agenda of the discussions between the two men, the security issue and in particular the fight against terrorism.

Mali.title: Bloody battles between al-Qaeda andISIS in the Sahel result in hundreds of deaths
Mali.summary: The joint border area between Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger is witnessing an unprecedented escalation in armed confrontations between ISIS in the Sahel and the group "Victory of Islam and Muslims" linked to Al-Qaeda, after the competition between the two parties for areas of influence and supply routes turned into bloody battles that left hundreds dead, amid indications of the spread of fighting to new areas in West Africa Last Monday, ISIS in the Sahel announced the killing of more than 400 fighters of the group "Victory of Islam and Muslims", including a number of its leaders, during battles that took place last…

Mali.title: Islamic State's military victory over its Al Qaeda rivals in Burkina Faso
Mali.summary: If the communication war rages between the two jihadist franchises on the balance sheet of the large-scale fighting that has occurred in recent days in the north of Burkina Faso, they attest, in any case, to a level of violence unprecedented between the two groups in the Sahel since the eruption of their rivalry in 2019 .

Mali.title: Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger: deadly clashes between rival factions in the Sahel of Al-Qaeda and the Islamic State
Mali.summary: Clashes on an unprecedented scale have been taking place for several weeks between the Sahelian branches of the jihadists of the Islamic State (ISIS) and Al-Qaeda (JNIM) in the border area straddling Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger . These fights are reaching an unprecedented level of violence, with hundreds of deaths claimed on both sides.

Niger.title: SCHOOL OF NON-COMMISSIONED OFFICERS OF BANANKORO: a new generation of military executives in the service of the nation
Niger.summary: The Minister Delegate to the Minister of Defence and Veterans Affairs, Major General Oumar DIARRA, chaired, on Friday, October 16, 2026, the graduation ceremony of the 20th promotion of the School of Non-Commissioned Officers (ESO) of Banankoro. Called "Late Chief Warrant Officer Mamadou DIARRA", for armoured weapons and cavalry, this promotion strengthens the strength of the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) .

Niger.title: Niger: the Human Rights Observatory with investigative powers
Niger.summary: An ordinance signed on 13 October 2026 establishes the missions, composition and functioning of the National Observatory for Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms (ONDH/LF). Presented as an independent administrative authority, the body will have its headquarters in Niamey and may have representations on the national territory The Observatory may receive complaints from victims, their beneficiaries or national human rights organisations.
